GainsBlock.maps_to: mad_science.py:101-105 `MadScienceCard.gains_block`, a property returning `self.tinker_type == CardType.SKILL` -- the same type-dependence the sibling `base_block` property (mad_science.py:97-99) already had
GainsBlock.issue: REVISED 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep re-audit, citations only -- verdict unchanged, gap still present): re-read mad_science.py in full against MadScience.cs; `gains_block` is still absent from the whole file after the file grew (188 lines now, was smaller at the 2026-07-26 audit) -- confirmed by grep, no match anywhere in sts2_rl/cards/mad_science.py. `public override bool GainsBlock => TinkerTimeType == CardType.Skill` (MadScience.cs:94) is TYPE-DEPENDENT; the sim never sets `gains_block` at all -- not in the class body and not in `configure` (mad_science.py:80-91, which sets `tinker_type`/`card_type`/`target_type`/`rider` but not this). So a Skill-configured Mad Science, which gains 8 block, reports `gains_block = False`. Observable through the Nimble enchantment, whose `can_enchant` gates on exactly this flag (cards/base.py:168-169 names Nimble as the reader, comment: "Nimble's CanEnchant gates on it"): in the game Nimble accepts a Skill Mad Science and in the sim it refuses. DORMANT only if Nimble is unreachable -- it is a ported enchantment (enchantments.py), and Mad Science reaches the deck from the ported Tinker Time event, so this is LIVE for the Skill configuration, on BOTH driver paths (RL-training and conformance-replay both run the same `can_enchant` gate). Note the sim DOES get the related `base_block` right, via an overriding property that returns the block only for the Skill type (mad_science.py:97-99) -- so the type-dependence was clearly understood and this one flag was missed. REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_shared_enchantments.py:52` -- `test_nimble_requires_gains_block` is the existing gate for this attribute; it asserts `make_card("entrench").gains_block` and `not make_card("feel_no_pain").gains_block`. It has no Mad Science case, so the fix (setting `gains_block` from the configured type) should add one there rather than a new file.
GainsBlock.rationale: FIXED 2026-08-04. Was a LIVE gap: `gains_block` sat at the `Card` base-class False default (cards/base.py:169), never set in the class body or in `configure`, so a Skill-configured Mad Science (which gains 8 block) reported False while C#'s `GainsBlock => TinkerTimeType == CardType.Skill` (MadScience.cs:94) reports True. Observable through Nimble, whose CanEnchant gates on exactly this flag (Nimble.cs:8-14, sim enchantments.py:581): the game accepted a Skill Mad Science and the sim refused it. Now a property mirroring the C# expression, so all three configurations agree: Skill True, Attack and Power False. REGRESSION TEST: test/test_shared_enchantments.py `test_nimble_accepts_a_skill_mad_science_only` -- asserts the flag and Nimble's verdict for each of the three tinker types; it FAILED before the fix (Skill reported False) and passes after.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Event, TargetType.AnyEnemy, shouldShowInCardLibrary: false)` (MadScience.cs:167-170) == cost 1 / ATTACK / EVENT / ANY_ENEMY defaults. `shouldShowInCardLibrary: false` is a compendium-UI flag with no sim counterpart and no gameplay effect. `configure` then overwrites type and target.

CanonicalVars.rationale: All ELEVEN C# vars are accounted for (MadScience.cs:96-109), which makes this the most var-dense card in the pool: DamageVar 12 -> `_damage`, BlockVar 8 -> `_block`, and the nine rider amounts as module constants with matching values -- SappingWeak 2, SappingVulnerable 2, ViolenceHits 3, ChokingDamage 6, EnergizedEnergy 2, WisdomCards 3, ExpertiseStrength 2, ExpertiseDexterity 2, CuriousReduction 1 (mad_science.py:32-40). The two printed vars are exposed through overriding `base_damage` / `base_block` properties that return them only for the matching type (mad_science.py:93-99), which is more faithful than a plain attribute would be. The rider constants are module-level rather than instance vars, so `magic_number` does not surface them -- acceptable, since C# keys them by name rather than treating any one as the card's headline number.

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The RIDER guard `if target.is_gone: return` is deleted (mad_science.py). ExecuteRider is called from OnPlay's tail with no liveness test of any kind (MadScience.cs:210-214, :267-294), so the Sapping and Choking powers are gated only by CanReceivePowers. The card's own `if not target.is_gone:` is DELETED and PowerCmd.apply now carries the WHOLE of `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-322): `cmds.can_receive_powers` is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)`, and `Creature.is_removed_from_combat` (creatures.py) is `is_gone and not retained_after_death` -- the sim's expression of `CombatState == null`, since it never drops a corpse from `enemies` (conformance addresses enemies by index). The two edits are a MATCHED PAIR: round 6 had wired only the ShouldAllowHitting half here, so deleting the card guard on its own would have powered the ordinary corpse that CreatureCmd.cs:523-531 removes. Pinned by test/test_can_receive_powers.py -- ordinary corpse refused, removal-vetoed corpse powered, mid-revival corpse still refused. The per-hit break in the Violence loop STAYS and is now justified in the file: it is AttackCommand's own `Attacker.IsDead` / empty-`validTargets` pair (AttackCommand.cs:538-550), not a sim invention. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable the entry proposed -- a Vicious draw off a retained corpse -- is not reachable in the sim's SHIPPED content, and the enumeration is the finding. Every sim producer of a retained corpse also makes it unhittable for as long as it lasts (IllusionPower.cs:95-105, AdaptablePower.cs:68-78 and ReattachPower.cs:74-86 each pair the removal veto with ShouldAllowHitting), the sole exception being a Decimillipede segment killed with every other segment already down -- and that ends the combat, so PowerCmd.Apply's own IsEnding guard (PowerCmd.cs:69-72) swallows it first. The game's third case, PainfulStabsPower.cs:29-32 on Test Subject phase 2, retains WITHOUT vetoing hits and the sim's PainfulStabsPower omits that override; recorded here rather than fixed, because it is not this entry's line. The code is now the source's shape either way.  The text it replaced read: The type dispatch, every rider effect and every amount are faithful, and the rider-per-type partition is correct: C# handles Expertise/Curious/Improvement inside `ExecutePower` (MadScience.cs:232-248) and Sapping/Choking/Energized/Wisdom/Chaos in `ExecuteRider` (267-294), which the sim reorganises into `_play_attack` (sapping, choking), `_play_skill` (energized, wisdom, chaos) and `_play_power` (expertise, curious, improvement) -- the same nine effects, and `configure` enforces the per-type rider partition (mad_science.py:123-124) that C# leaves to Tinker Time. The Violence hit count is right (3 vs 1, MadScience.cs:218). The Chaos rider even gets the RNG STREAM right, branching on `crng.is_parity` and using `crng.card_gen` (mad_science.py:190-194) -- the correct shape that card/discovery, card/distraction, card/jack_of_all_trades, card/jackpot, card/metamorphosis and card/hidden_gem all miss. THE DIVERGENCE is the sim's two extra liveness guards: `if target.is_gone or ctx.player.is_dead: break` between the Violence hits (151-152) and `if target.is_gone: return` before the Sapping / Choking riders (154-155). The per-hit break is the correct analogue of AttackCommand's own breaks and carries nothing; the RIDER guard does. C# applies the power unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse. The two agree for an ordinary kill (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, and removal happens at 523-525) and diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower and any listener that fires on a power landing regardless of target liveness. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. One more nuance recorded rather than verdicted: the Chaos rider uses `set_free_this_turn` where C# calls `SetToFreeThisTurn()` (MadScience.cs:287) -- the same verb -- and adds to hand via `add_to_hand` where C# uses `CardPileCmd.Add(cardModel, PileType.Hand)` (288), the pile-verb difference the creature_card_cmds seam owns.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Innate)` (MadScience.cs:252) == `self.innate = True`, and this card DOES re-seed the flag in `_init_vars` (`self.innate = False`, mad_science.py:75, with a comment saying why), so `downgrade()` restores it -- `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` does not list mad_science. The correct pattern, unlike card/aggression, card/hello_world and card/juggling.
